--- title: "Hands-on_Ex07a" author: "JUNCHEN LI" date: "June 2,2026" date-modified: "last-modified" format: html editor: visual execute: eval: true echo: true warning: false freeze: True --- # 1 Overview In this hands-on exercise, you will learn how to model, analyse and visualise network data using R. By the end of this hands-on exercise, you will be able to: - create graph object data frames, manipulate them using appropriate functions of *dplyr*, *lubridate*, and *tidygraph*, - build network graph visualisation using appropriate functions of *ggraph*, - compute network geometrics using *tidygraph*, - build advanced graph visualisation by incorporating the network geometrics, and - build interactive network visualisation using *visNetwork* package. ## 2 Getting Started (Ex) ### 2.1 Installing and launching R packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(igraph, tidygraph, ggraph, visNetwork, lubridate, clock, tidyverse, graphlayouts, concaveman, ggforce) ``` ::: ### 2.2 Importing network data from files ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_nodes <- read_csv("data/GAStech_email_node.csv") GAStech_edges <- read_csv("data/GAStech_email_edge-v2.csv") ``` ::: ### 2.3 Reviewing the imported data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(GAStech_edges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 9,063 Columns: 8 $ source 43, 43, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 44, 26, 26, 26… $ target 41, 40, 51, 52, 53, 45, 44, 46, 48, 49, 47, 54, 27, "Lucas.Alcazar", "Felix.Resumir", "Hideki.Coc… ``` ::: ::: ### 2.4 Wrangling time ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_edges <- GAStech_edges %>% mutate(SendDate = dmy(SentDate)) %>% mutate(Weekday = wday(SentDate, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)) ``` ::: ### 2.5 Wrangling attributes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_edges_aggregated <- GAStech_edges %>% filter(MainSubject == "Work related") %>% group_by(source, target, Weekday) %>% summarise(Weight = n()) %>% filter(source!=target) %>% filter(Weight > 1) %>% ungroup() ``` ::: ## 3 Creating network objects using tidygraph ### 3.1 Using tbl_graph() to build tidygraph data model. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = GAStech_nodes, edges = GAStech_edges_aggregated, directed = TRUE) ``` ::: ### 3.2 Reviewing {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "fr") + geom_edge_link(aes()) + geom_node_point(aes()) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ### 4.5 Modifying network nodes ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes()) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department, size = 3)) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ### 4.6 Modifying edges ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department), size = 3) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ## 5 Creating facet graphs ### 5.1 Working with facet_edges() ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set_graph_style() g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department), size = 2) g + facet_edges(~Weekday) ``` ::: ::: ### 5.2 Working with facet_edges() ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set_graph_style() g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department), size = 2) + theme(legend.position = 'bottom') g + facet_edges(~Weekday) ``` ::: ::: ### 5.3 A framed facet graph ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set_graph_style() g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department), size = 2) g + facet_edges(~Weekday) + th_foreground(foreground = "grey80", border = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = 'bottom') ``` ::: ::: ### 5.4 Working with facet_nodes() ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set_graph_style() g <- ggraph(GAStech_graph, layout = "nicely") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department), size = 2) g + facet_nodes(~Department)+ th_foreground(foreground = "grey80", border = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = 'bottom') ``` ::: ::: ## 6 Network Metrics Analysis ### 6.1 Computing centrality indices ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-29-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- GAStech_graph %>% mutate(betweenness_centrality = centrality_betweenness()) %>% ggraph(layout = "fr") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department, size=betweenness_centrality)) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ### 6.2 Visualising network metrics ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-31-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- GAStech_graph %>% ggraph(layout = "fr") + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(colour = Department, size = centrality_betweenness())) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ### 6.3 Visualising Community ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-33-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- GAStech_graph %>% mutate(community = as.factor( group_edge_betweenness( weights = Weight, directed = TRUE))) %>% ggraph(layout = "fr") + geom_edge_link( aes( width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width( range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point( aes(colour = community)) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ::: callout-note Please be reminded that you must to install and include ggforce and concaveman packages before running the code chunk below. ::: ::: panel-tabset #### The plot 2 ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-35-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- GAStech_graph %>% activate(nodes) %>% mutate(community = as.factor( group_optimal(weights = Weight)), betweenness_measure = centrality_betweenness()) %>% ggraph(layout = "fr") + geom_mark_hull( aes(x, y, group = community, fill = community), alpha = 0.2, expand = unit(0.3, "cm"), # Expand radius = unit(0.3, "cm") # Smoothness ) + geom_edge_link(aes(width=Weight), alpha=0.2) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 5)) + geom_node_point(aes(fill = Department, size = betweenness_measure), color = "black", shape = 21) g + theme_graph() ``` ::: ::: ## 7 Building Interactive Network Graph with visNetwork ### 7.1 Data preparation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_edges_aggregated <- GAStech_edges %>% left_join(GAStech_nodes, by = c("sourceLabel" = "label")) %>% rename(from = id) %>% left_join(GAStech_nodes, by = c("targetLabel" = "label")) %>% rename(to = id) %>% filter(MainSubject == "Work related") %>% group_by(from, to) %>% summarise(weight = n()) %>% filter(from!=to) %>% filter(weight > 1) %>% ungroup() ``` ::: ### 7.2 Plotting the first interactive network graph ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} visNetwork(GAStech_nodes, GAStech_edges_aggregated) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 7.3 Working with layout ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} visNetwork(GAStech_nodes, GAStech_edges_aggregated) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") ``` ::: ::: ### 7.4 Working with visual attributes - Nodes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} GAStech_nodes <- GAStech_nodes %>% rename(group = Department) ``` ::: ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} visNetwork(GAStech_nodes, GAStech_edges_aggregated) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visLegend() %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: ::: ### 7.5 Working with visual attributes - Edges ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} visNetwork(GAStech_nodes, GAStech_edges_aggregated) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visEdges(arrows = "to", smooth = list(enabled = TRUE, type = "curvedCW")) %>% visLegend() %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: ::: ### 7.6 Interactivity ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} visNetwork(GAStech_nodes, GAStech_edges_aggregated) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visOptions(highlightNearest = TRUE, nodesIdSelection = TRUE) %>% visLegend() %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: ::: ## Self Trying ### 8.1 Analysis objective In this self-trying section, I focus on the stronger work-related communication links during weekdays. The purpose is to reduce visual noise and identify employees who play important roles in the internal communication network. I use a higher edge threshold, calculate multiple centrality measures, compare the top employees, detect communities, and create an interactive graph. ### 8.2 Preparing a focused weekday network The original graph includes work-related email links from all days. In this analysis, I only retain weekday emails and communication links with at least three messages. This makes the network easier to interpret and highlights stronger work relationships. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create a node table that works after the earlier visNetwork renaming step self_nodes <- GAStech_nodes if ("Department" %in% names(self_nodes)) { self_nodes <- self_nodes %>% rename(group = Department) } # Keep stronger weekday work-related email links self_edges <- GAStech_edges %>% filter(MainSubject == "Work related") %>% filter(Weekday %in% c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday")) %>% group_by(source, target) %>% summarise(Weight = n(), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(source != target) %>% filter(Weight >= 3) # Build a new directed network object self_graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = self_nodes, edges = self_edges, directed = TRUE) self_graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tbl_graph: 54 nodes and 0 edges # # A rooted forest with 54 trees # # Node Data: 54 × 4 (active) id label group Title 1 1 Mat.Bramar Administration Assistant to CEO 2 2 Anda.Ribera Administration Assistant to CFO 3 3 Rachel.Pantanal Administration Assistant to CIO 4 4 Linda.Lagos Administration Assistant to COO 5 5 Ruscella.Mies.Haber Administration Assistant to Engineering Group Mana… 6 6 Carla.Forluniau Administration Assistant to IT Group Manager 7 7 Cornelia.Lais Administration Assistant to Security Group Manager 8 44 Kanon.Herrero Security Badging Office 9 45 Varja.Lagos Security Badging Office 10 46 Stenig.Fusil Security Building Control # ℹ 44 more rows # # Edge Data: 0 × 3 # ℹ 3 variables: from , to , Weight ``` ::: ::: ### 8.3 Identifying important employees with centrality metrics Degree centrality measures the number of direct connections. In-degree indicates how many communication links an employee receives, while out-degree indicates how many links an employee sends. Betweenness centrality identifies employees who act as bridges between different parts of the organisation. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} self_graph_metrics <- self_graph %>% activate(nodes) %>% mutate(in_degree = centrality_degree(mode = "in"), out_degree = centrality_degree(mode = "out"), total_degree = in_degree + out_degree, betweenness = centrality_betweenness(), key_employee = if_else( rank(-betweenness, ties.method = "min") <= 5, label, "" )) ``` ::: ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-50-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggraph(self_graph_metrics, layout = "fr") + geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), alpha = 0.18, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"))) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 3)) + geom_node_point(aes(size = total_degree, colour = group), alpha = 0.9) + geom_node_text(aes(label = key_employee), repel = TRUE, size = 3) + theme_graph() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + labs(title = "Key Employees in the Weekday Work Email Network", subtitle = "Node size represents total degree; labels show the top five bridge employees", colour = "Department", size = "Total degree", edge_width = "Email frequency") ``` ::: ::: ### 8.4 Comparing the top bridge employees The following table ranks employees by betweenness centrality. Employees with higher values may be important coordinators because they connect different communication paths. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} self_top_employees <- self_graph_metrics %>% activate(nodes) %>% as_tibble() %>% arrange(desc(betweenness)) %>% select(label, group, in_degree, out_degree, total_degree, betweenness) %>% slice_head(n = 10) knitr::kable(self_top_employees, digits = 2, caption = "Top 10 employees ranked by betweenness centrality") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Top 10 employees ranked by betweenness centrality |label |group | in_degree| out_degree| total_degree| betweenness| |:-------------------|:--------------|---------:|----------:|------------:|-----------:| |Mat.Bramar |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Anda.Ribera |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Rachel.Pantanal |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Linda.Lagos |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Ruscella.Mies.Haber |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Carla.Forluniau |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Cornelia.Lais |Administration | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Kanon.Herrero |Security | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Varja.Lagos |Security | 0| 0| 0| 0| |Stenig.Fusil |Security | 0| 0| 0| 0| ::: ::: ### 8.5 Detecting communication communities I also apply edge-betweenness community detection. This helps identify groups of employees who communicate more closely with each other. The shaded hulls show the detected communities, while node colours still represent departments. This makes it possible to compare formal departments with actual communication groups. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} self_graph_community <- self_graph_metrics %>% activate(nodes) %>% mutate(community = as.factor( group_edge_betweenness(weights = Weight, directed = TRUE) )) ``` ::: ::: panel-tabset #### The plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex07a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-54-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### The Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggraph(self_graph_community, layout = "fr") + geom_mark_hull(aes(x, y, group = community, fill = community), alpha = 0.15, expand = unit(0.25, "cm"), radius = unit(0.20, "cm")) + geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), alpha = 0.16) + scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 3)) + geom_node_point(aes(size = total_degree, fill = group), colour = "black", shape = 21, alpha = 0.9) + theme_graph() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + labs(title = "Communication Communities in the Weekday Work Email Network", subtitle = "Hull areas represent detected communities; node fill represents department", fill = "Department", size = "Total degree", edge_width = "Email frequency") ``` ::: ::: ### 8.6 Building an interactive version The final graph is interactive. Users can select a node, highlight nearby employees, and view each employee's department, community, degree score, and betweenness score. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} self_vis_nodes <- self_graph_community %>% activate(nodes) %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(department = group, group = paste0("Community ", community), value = total_degree, title = paste0( "Employee: ", label, "
Department: ", department, "
Community: ", community, "
Total degree: ", total_degree, "
Betweenness: ", round(betweenness, 2) )) %>% select(id, label, group, value, title) self_vis_edges <- self_edges %>% rename(from = source, to = target) %>% mutate(value = Weight, title = paste0("Number of emails: ", Weight)) visNetwork(self_vis_nodes, self_vis_edges) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visEdges(arrows = "to", smooth = list(enabled = TRUE, type = "curvedCW")) %>% visOptions(highlightNearest = TRUE, nodesIdSelection = TRUE) %>% visLegend() %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 8.7 Interpretation This analysis focuses on strong weekday work-related email connections. The network graph can reveal employees who are highly connected and employees who act as bridges between communication groups. The community graph can also show whether actual email communication patterns follow the formal departmental structure. If an employee has high betweenness centrality but only a moderate degree score, the employee may still be important because they connect otherwise separated groups.
